## Problem 1: NY NOAA

### Load `ny_noaa` Dataset

```{r}
library(p8105.datasets)
data("ny_noaa")
```

### Data Description

The `ny_noaa` dataset provides daily weather data from `r min(pull(ny_noaa, date))` to `r max(pull(ny_noaa, date))` in different locations in New York, resulting in `r nrow(ny_noaa)` total observations. There are `r ncol(ny_noaa)` variables in the dataset, including the weather station ID (`id`), daily precipitation (`prcp`), daily snowfall (`snow`), daily snow depth (`snwd`), and maximum and minimum daily temperature (`tmax`, `tmin`). Among all observation in the dataset, there is `r ((sum(is.na(pull(ny_noaa, id))))/(nrow(ny_noaa)))*100`% and `r ((sum(is.na(pull(ny_noaa, date))))/(nrow(ny_noaa)))*100`% missing data in regards to weather station ID (`id`) and date (`date`) of observation, respectively. However, there is more extensive missing data in regard to the other weather-related values. Specifically, among all observations in the `ny_noaa` dataset `r round(((sum(is.na(pull(ny_noaa, prcp))))/(nrow(ny_noaa)))*100, 2)`% of precipitation (`prcp`) data is missing, `r round(((sum(is.na(pull(ny_noaa, snow))))/(nrow(ny_noaa)))*100, 2)`% of snowfall (`snow`) data is missing, `r round(((sum(is.na(pull(ny_noaa, snwd))))/(nrow(ny_noaa)))*100, 2)`% of snow depth (`snwd`) data is missing, `r round(((sum(is.na(pull(ny_noaa, tmax))))/(nrow(ny_noaa)))*100, 2)`% of maximum temperature (`tmax`) data is missing, and `r round(((sum(is.na(pull(ny_noaa, tmin))))/(nrow(ny_noaa)))*100, 2)`% of minimum temperature (`tmin`) data is missing.

### Data Cleaning

```{r}
noaa = ny_noaa |>
  separate(date, into = c("year", "month", "day"), "-") |>
  mutate(
    prcp = as.numeric(prcp)/10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax)/10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin)/10
    )
```

```{r}
snow_freq_df = noaa |>
  group_by(snow) |>
  summarise(n_obs = n()) |>
  mutate(snow_freq_rank = min_rank(desc(n_obs)))
```

For snowfall, the most common value of ``r pull(filter(snow_freq_df, snow_freq_rank == 1), snow)`` mm occurred across `r pull(filter(snow_freq_df, snow_freq_rank == 1), n_obs)` observations. This is due to the fact that it does not snow on most days of the year and usually only during certain months of the year. The second most common value of ``r pull(filter(snow_freq_df, snow_freq_rank == 2), snow)`` occurred across `r pull(filter(snow_freq_df, snow_freq_rank == 2), n_obs)` observations. This is due to the fact that some weather stations only recorded precipitation data.

### Average `tmax` Plot

```{r}
noaa |>
  filter(month == "01" | month == "07") |>
  group_by(id, month, year) |>
  summarize(mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm=TRUE)) |>
  mutate(
    month = case_match(month, 
                      "01" ~ "January", 
                      "07" ~ "July")
    ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(month ~ .) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature in January and July",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average maximum daily temperature (°C)",
    caption = "Data from the ny_noaa dataset") +
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = c(1982, 1984, 1986, 1988, 1990, 1992, 1994, 1996, 1998, 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2008, 2010), 
    labels = c("1982", "1984", "1986", "1988", "1990", "1992", "1994", "1996", "1998", "2000", "2002", "2004", "2006", "2008", "2010"))
```

Visually inspecting the maximum temperature plot indicates that January is generally colder with lower `mean_tmax` temperatures and July is warmer with higher `mean_tmax` temperatures. There are noticeable outliers with one weather station reporting on average a cold July in 1988 of roughly 14 degrees Celcius `mean_tmax`, as well as one weather station reporting a particularly cold January in 1982 on average of roughly -4 degrees Celsius `mean_tmax`.

### `tmax` vs `tmin` Plot & Snowfall Distribution Plot

```{r}
ggp_tmax_tmin = noaa |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_hex() +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature Plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maxiumum daily temperature (°C)",
    caption = "Data from the ny_noaa dataset") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggp_snow_ridge = noaa |> 
  filter(snow > 0 & snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = snow, y = year)) + 
  geom_density_ridges(scale = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual Distribution of Daily Snowfall (0-100mm)",
    x = "Snowfall (mm)",
    y = "Year",
    caption = "Data from the ny_noaa dataset")

ggp_tmax_tmin + ggp_snow_ridge
```

## Problem 2: MIMS

### Load, tidy and merge `mims_demos` and `mims_accel`

```{r}
mims_demos = 
  read_csv("data/nhanes_covar.csv", 
           skip = 4,
           na = c("NA")) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    seqn = as.character(seqn),
    sex = case_match(sex, 
                     1 ~ "male", 
                     2 ~ "female"),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("male", "female")),
    education = case_match(education, 
                           1 ~ "less than high school",
                           2 ~ "high school equivalent",
                           3 ~ "more than high school"),
    education = factor(education, 
                       levels = c("less than high school", 
                                  "high school equivalent", 
                                  "more than high school")
                       )
    )

mims_accel = 
  read_csv("data/nhanes_accel.csv")|>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(seqn = as.character(seqn)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    min1:min1440,
    names_to = "min", 
    names_prefix = "min",
    values_to = "mims")
```

### Merge `mims_demos` and `mims_accel` into `mims` 

```{r}
mims = left_join(mims_demos, mims_accel, by = "seqn") |>
       select(seqn, min, mims, everything()) |>
       filter(age > 20 & !is.na(sex) & !is.na(age) & 
              !is.na(bmi) & !is.na(education))
```

### N men and women by education

```{r}
mims |> 
  group_by(education, sex) |>
  summarise(count = n()) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

### Age distribution for men and women by education

```{r}
mims |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age, fill = sex)) + 
  geom_density(alpha = .4, adjust = .5, color = "blue") +
  facet_grid(education ~ .) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Age for Men and Women by Education",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Density",
    caption = "Data from nhanes dataset")
```
